title: Initiating a project: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Apply the seven initiation activities to a scenario, from agreeing tailoring to requesting authorization, and use the RACI for preparing the full business case.
question: The project manager updates the outline business case with the costs and timescales from the new project plan. Which role should be accountable for the 'prepare the full business case' activity?

teach.body: Formally: initiating a project establishes solid foundations so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing to significant spend (15.1). It starts with the initiation notice and ends with a request for project authorization. In plain English: decide how the method fits, how the project will be run and controlled, what it will cost and take, then package it all as the PID and ask the board for the go-ahead.

teach.caption: Once the approaches are defined, the controls and the project plan can follow; the full business case needs the plan's time and cost.

teach.h: Key action and output of each activity
head: Activity
Key recommended action
Output
rows: Document and agree how the method is tailored
Derive from business standards and the PPD; seek lessons
Agree the board's control and the PM's control of team work
Build the product and work breakdowns and flow
Add plan time and cost, aggregated risks
PM contacts the board, meeting optional
teach.caption: The registers in the project log (risk, issue, quality, product) are also set up during initiation.

teach.h: RACI: prepare the full business case (tab 15.2)
head: Role
Letter
Meaning here
teach.caption: This pattern (PM responsible, executive accountable, assurance consulted) recurs across the processes, but check the cells for the specific activity before answering.

teach.h: The nine management approaches and their practice
teach.caption: All nine are agreed in 'agree the management approaches' and sit in or alongside the PID.

teach.h: The PID is cross-checked, then baselined
teach.body: In 'assemble the project initiation documentation' the PM cross-checks the parts so they are compatible (for example, benefits reviews in the benefits approach match the controls and the communication approach). The version used to gain authorization is baselined and placed under change control; it becomes the basis for judging the project at closure.

items: Tailoring first: it shapes how every later product is written.
Approaches next: controls and the plan depend on how risk, quality, issues and data will be managed.
Plan before full business case: the case needs the plan's time and cost and the aggregated risks.
PID last, then the request: the board authorizes a complete, consistent package.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Single Point of Access (S3)
teach.body: At Wenmoor Community Health, Ellie Chandran adapts PRINCE2 reports to the trust's quality improvement templates and gets the board's agreement in writing. She agrees the approaches, seeking lessons on patient data sharing for the digital and data approach. She sets monthly highlight reports and fortnightly checkpoints, prepares the project plan, then updates the business case with its costs; executive Karen Lindqvist approves it after Ellie consults the head of internal audit. Ellie cross-checks the PID and emails the board to request authorization.

teach.text: Classic traps: the business layer is NOT involved in preparing the full business case (executive accountable, PM responsible, assurance consulted). Specific risks go in the risk register, not the risk management approach. No delivery work, such as starting a pilot, begins before the board authorizes the project.

items: Seven activities: tailoring, management approaches, controls, project plan, full business case, PID, request authorization.
Full business case: executive A, PM R, assurance C, business layer not involved.
Approaches come from business standards and the PPD; lessons are sought for them.
The PID is cross-checked, baselined and put under change control; authorization can be requested without a formal meeting.

summary: You can now recognize each initiation activity in a scenario, state its recommended action and output, and judge whether it was carried out as the manual recommends. You can also apply the RACI for preparing the full business case.

A.q: Wenmoor Community Health is initiating its Single Point of Access project. The project manager has finished the project plan and now updates the outline business case with the plan's costs and timescales and the aggregated risks from the project log. Which role should be accountable for this activity?
A.why: Tab 15.2: the executive is accountable for 'prepare the full business case', approving the updated case (15.4.5, 15.6).

whyNot.0: The business layer is not involved in this activity.
whyNot.2: The project manager is responsible: she prepares the case for the executive's approval.

A.q: Near the end of Wenmoor's initiation, the project manager combines the management approaches, project plan, controls and full business case, and checks that the timing of benefits reviews fits the controls and the communication approach. Which activity is she carrying out, and why is it appropriate?
options: Establish project controls, because it sets how the board will monitor benefits
Agree the management approaches, because the benefits approach is one of them
Request project authorization, because the board needs a consistent package
Assemble the PID, because the parts are cross-checked to make sure they fit
A.why: Assemble the project initiation documentation includes a cross-check of the information in its parts to ensure they are compatible (15.4.6).

whyNot.0: Controls are set up earlier; checking consistency across all the parts is part of assembling the PID.
whyNot.1: The approaches are agreed earlier; this is checking them against the other parts.
whyNot.2: The request comes after the PID is assembled; the cross-check belongs to assembling it.

A.q: During Wenmoor's initiation, the project manager agrees with the board that it will receive monthly highlight reports and that the triage hub team leaders will send her fortnightly checkpoint reports. Which activity is this?
A.why: Establish project controls agrees the level and mechanism of the board's control after initiation and the PM's control over the team managers' work (15.4.3).

whyNot.1: Tailoring adapts the method itself; the reporting levels here are project controls.
whyNot.2: The project plan sets out products, timescales and costs, not the reporting regime.
whyNot.3: The approaches define procedures such as risk and quality; controls set how the board and PM keep control.

B.q: Wenmoor's head of internal audit provides project assurance for the Single Point of Access board. The project manager is preparing the full business case. How should project assurance be involved in 'prepare the full business case'?
B.why: Tab 15.2: project assurance is consulted in 'prepare the full business case'; the PM prepares it in consultation with assurance for the executive's approval (15.6).

whyNot.1: Assurance is consulted before the case is finalized, not just told afterwards.

B.q: During Wenmoor's initiation, the project manager learns that a neighbouring trust had problems sharing patient data on a similar referral project. She seeks their lessons on keeping referral data secure and private. In which initiation activity should these lessons be used?
B.why: In agree the management approaches the PM seeks lessons related to the approaches; data security and privacy belong in the digital and data management approach (15.4.2, 11.5).

whyNot.1: The business case is about justification, not how data will be kept secure.
whyNot.2: Tailoring adapts the method; data security rules belong in an approach.
whyNot.3: Controls set reporting and decision levels, not data protection.

B.q: Wenmoor no longer has a project management office, and its staff are used to quality improvement templates. The project manager adapts the PRINCE2 report formats to those templates and records the deviation, which the board agrees in writing. Which activity is this?
B.why: Agree the tailoring requirements adapts the method to internal and external factors; how it is tailored must be documented and agreed (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Controls set the level of control, not how the method's products are adapted.
whyNot.1: The PID records the tailoring, but deciding and agreeing it is the tailoring activity.
whyNot.2: The approaches define procedures for areas such as risk and quality, not report formats.

C.q: Wenmoor's project team can usually meet only online at lunchtime. When the PID is complete, the project manager emails it to the board and asks for authority to deliver the project, without calling a meeting. Is this an appropriate application of the 'request project authorization' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM baselines the PID before asking the board
Yes, because the request can be made with or without a meeting
No, because the board must meet in person to approve the PID
No, because the executive should request authorization
C.why: To finish initiation the PM contacts the board to request authorization; this can be done with or without a formal meeting (15.4.7, 14.4.1).

whyNot.0: The version used to gain authorization is baselined, but that does not explain whether email is acceptable.
whyNot.2: A formal meeting is not required.
whyNot.3: The project manager makes the request; the board, led by the executive, decides.

C.q: Wenmoor's head of nursing for Eastfield, the senior user, asks the project manager to open the triage hub in Eastfield next week because her team is overstretched. Initiation is half finished and the project has not been authorized. The project manager agrees. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the pilot is planned to take place in Eastfield in any case
Yes, because the senior user gives user-related direction
No, because delivery waits until the board authorizes the project
No, because the hub needs an exception plan before it opens
C.why: Initiation builds solid foundations before significant spend, and the project must be properly initiated and authorized before delivery work starts (15.1, 2.4).

whyNot.0: The pilot is planned, but for a later stage after authorization.
whyNot.1: The senior user can give direction, but not authority to start delivery before the project is authorized.
whyNot.3: No tolerance has been breached, so there is no exception plan; the issue is authorization.

C.q: While agreeing the management approaches, Wenmoor's project manager writes into the risk management approach that 'several Moorside GP practices may keep faxing referrals', with a named owner and a response. Is this an appropriate application of the 'agree the management approaches' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the risk approach is agreed during initiation
Yes, because early risks move here from the daily log
No, because risks are recorded in the business case
No, because specific risks belong in the risk register
C.why: The risk management approach describes the goals and procedure for risk management and does not include specific risks; those go in the risk register (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: The approach is agreed in initiation, but that does not make it the place for specific risks.
whyNot.1: Early risks move from the daily log to the risk register, not the approach.
whyNot.2: The business case summarizes major risks, but individual risks are recorded in the risk register.

reteach.title: Initiation as a build sequence
reteach.question: Can you put the seven initiation activities in a sensible order and say who owns the full business case?

blocks.body: First the rules: how the method is tailored and how risk, quality, issues, data, benefits and the rest will be managed. Then the numbers: controls, the project plan and the full business case built on it. Then the package: the cross-checked, baselined PID and the request to the board.

blocks.text: Full business case: the executive approves (A), the PM prepares (R), assurance is consulted (C); the business layer has no part.

explain.body: Agree the tailoring requirements documents and agrees how PRINCE2 or the business's standard method is adapted. Agree the management approaches derives the approaches from business standards and the users' quality and sustainability expectations in the PPD, using lessons from similar projects.

test.q: Wenmoor's project manager is drafting the quality management approach. What should the approaches be derived from?
options: The highlight reports from the first stage
The end stage report from the initiation stage
The detailed work packages for the pilot
Business standards and the users' expectations
test.why: The approaches are derived from business strategies, standards or practices the project must follow and the users' quality and sustainability expectations in the PPD (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: Highlight reports come later, during delivery stages.
whyNot.1: The end stage report comes at the end of initiation, after the approaches are agreed.
whyNot.2: Work packages are authorized in controlling a stage, after initiation.

explain.body: Establish project controls agrees how much control the board needs after initiation, by what mechanism, and how the PM will control the team managers' work. Prepare the project plan then sets out the products, timescales and costs, which the full business case will use.

rows.label: Example
values: Pilot in stage 3, roll-out in stage 4

test.q: Wenmoor's executive asks how much control the board will have once the project moves into its design stage. In which initiation activity should this be agreed?
test.why: Establish project controls agrees the board's level of control after initiation and the mechanism for it (15.4.3).

whyNot.0: The project plan covers products, time and cost, not the board's control mechanism.
whyNot.1: Tailoring adapts the method; the level of board control is a project control.
whyNot.3: The request asks for authority once controls and the rest of the PID are ready.

explain.body: The outline business case from starting up is updated with time and cost from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log. The PM is responsible, the executive accountable, project assurance consulted, and the business layer not involved.

test.q: Wenmoor's trust executive team has set the project's cost and time tolerances. The project manager is now preparing the full business case. How should the business layer be involved in this activity?
test.why: Tab 15.2: the business layer has no involvement in 'prepare the full business case' (15.6).

whyNot.0: Project assurance is the role consulted.

explain.body: The PID is cross-checked so its parts are compatible, and the version used to gain authorization is baselined and placed under change control. The PM then contacts the board to request authority to deliver the project, with or without a formal meeting.

test.q: Wenmoor's board has authorized the Single Point of Access project. What should happen to the version of the PID used to gain that authorization?
options: It is baselined and put under change control
It is replaced by the outline business case
It is archived until the closing stage begins
It is merged into the next stage plan
test.why: The PID version used to gain authorization must be baselined and placed under change control (15.4.6).

whyNot.1: The outline business case was superseded by the full case in the PID, not the other way round.
whyNot.2: The PID stays in use and is reviewed at stage boundaries; closing is not a stage either.
whyNot.3: Stage plans are separate products; the PID stays as the baseline.
